title: The armor of God (Ephesians 6:10–20)
hook: belt of truth, breastplate of righteousness, shoes of peace, shield of faith
tomorrow: how do you see a God nobody can see?

segments.voice: Yesterday, anger got a deadline, before the sun goes down, and the line was kind, tenderhearted. Today Paul reaches the end of his letter, in chains, talking about armor.

Game day: jersey on, laces double-knotted, the long walk out to the field. People suit up for hard things. At the end of Ephesians, Paul calls himself "an ambassador in bonds," a messenger in chains. A prisoner may well have had soldiers' gear in view every day. So Paul takes it piece by piece and dresses a whole church in armor that isn't made of metal. And the order he keeps giving isn't attack.
screen: `SUITING UP FOR HARD THINGS.` → `AN AMBASSADOR IN BONDS.` → `ARMOR THAT ISN'T METAL.`

segments.voice: Today's question: who is the real enemy? Paul opens, "be strong in the Lord, and in the power of his might." Borrowed strength. "Put on the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil. For we wrestle not against flesh and blood." The neighbor is not the enemy. Then the pieces: a belt of truth, the breastplate of righteousness, feet ready with "the gospel of peace," the shield of faith, the helmet of salvation. Here's one to tell a friend: the only blade in the whole list is "the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God," and the shoes are for carrying peace. And the verb is stand: "having done all, to stand." Nobody is told to charge. A neighbor tradition says something close, in its own words. The Buddhist Dhammapada, in Max Müller's translation: "If one man conquer in battle a thousand times thousand men, and if another conquer himself, he is the greatest of conquerors." That's the shared ground: the hardest fight isn't against other people. And the honest difference: Paul's armor is God's, put on by people who ask for strength from the Lord. The Dhammapada's victory is over oneself, and Buddhist teaching doesn't center on a creator God who arms you. Two paths, both pointing the battle inward.
screen: `WE WRESTLE NOT AGAINST FLESH AND BLOOD.` · `ONE BLADE: THE WORD OF GOD.` · `THE DHAMMAPADA: CONQUER HIMSELF.` · `THE DIFFERENCE: GOD'S ARMOR.` · then, large: `STAND.`

segments.voice: Pick one piece for tomorrow morning: truth, peace or faith. Say its name out loud once, slowly, as if fastening it on like a belt or a shoe. Then sit tall, feet flat on the floor, and simply hold your ground until the bell.
The armor of God. Paul's picture of strength borrowed from God, worn for standing firm, not for attacking anyone.
Keep this line: stand, and having done all, to stand, in borrowed strength. Rest easy tonight.

howItsDone: Some Christians name a piece of the armor of God as they get dressed in the morning, and some children learn the passage piece by piece in Sunday school.

fork.setup: your little brother says the armor of God means Christians should be ready to go after people. what do Paul's verbs actually say?
options: stand, withstand, and having done all, to stand: hold your ground.
charge: the sword means going on the attack first.
hide: the shield means staying out of sight of trouble.
fork.reveal: the armor is for standing: stand against the wiles of the devil… and having done all, to stand. nobody in the passage is told to charge.

chat.says: supper's tomorrow, i'm shaking. nia's world lit book says the hardest fight is with yourself. same as my armor verse?
options: Alike, not the same. Neither fight is with people. Paul's armor is God's; her book means conquering yourself.
Exactly the same. Every religion teaches the same thing about God, just in other words.
Totally different. Buddhists fight themselves; Christians fight the people against them.
chat.meaning: Ephesians: we wrestle not against flesh and blood. The Dhammapada: conquering oneself is the greatest victory. Shared: the fight isn't other people. Different: Paul's strength is God's.

Dhammapada.meaning: an early Buddhist collection of the Buddha's sayings

Buddhist.meaning: of the path that follows the teaching of the Buddha

ambassador in bonds.meaning: Paul's name for himself: a messenger in chains

Max Müller.meaning: a scholar whose English Dhammapada is in the public domain
